speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific movements you are experiencing and tell me if they started suddenly or gradually. When did these symptoms first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very helpful context. Now, when you perform tasks like buttoning a shirt or brushing your teeth, do you feel an involuntary urge to keep your limbs in a fixed position, or do you experience repetitive, rhythmic movements?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of restlessness, fidgeting, and repetitive crossing/uncrossing of your legs are highly suggestive of Akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To confirm this, I will check your vital signs and request a clinical movement assessment. REQUEST TEST: Vital_Signs; REQUEST IMAGES: Neurological_Exam_Video

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital_Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood_Pressure 120/80 mmHg, Heart_Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory_Rate 14 breaths/min; Neurological_Examination: Mental_Status Alert and oriented, psychotic symptoms improved, Cranial_Nerves Intact, Motor Normal tone and strength, Sensory Intact, Coordination Normal, Gait Normal but patient exhibits inability to sit still with frequent pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the vital signs and neurological exam confirming an inability to sit still with frequent pacing in a patient recently treated with risperidone, the clinical picture strongly supports a specific medication-induced condition.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Akathisia secondary to Risperidone.
